plan: In a single-round auction with rational bidders, the dominant strategy is to bid close to, but not exceeding, my private value. Since I value the item at $14, I want to bid strategically to maximize potential profit. A bid slightly below my true value reduces the risk of paying more than the item is worth to me. I'll bid $13.7 to create a small buffer while still having a good chance of winning.

In a first-price sealed bid auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below one's private value. Since my value is $34, I want to maximize potential profit. Given the $0-$49 uniform distribution, a strategic bid around 80-90% of my value (around $27-$31) balances winning probability and potential profit margin. I'll aim to bid just low enough to potentially win while preserving profit.

In a single-round auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically based on my private value. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, I want to bid close to my true value to maximize potential profit. My value is $33, so I'll bid slightly below that to create some potential profit margin. A bid around $32.5 seems rational - high enough to likely win, but leaving some potential profit if the second-highest bid is low.
